movie_title: Einstein's twin paradox explained - Amber Stuver
introduction: Follow two astronauts into outer space to explore time dilation and Einstein’s theory of relativity

vocabulary.definition: a seemingly absurd or contradictory statement or proposition which when investigated may prove to be well-founded or true
vocabulary.example: The time travel paradox suggests that changing events in the past can have unexpected consequences in the present.

vocabulary.definition: lack of equality or equivalence between parts or aspects of something; lack of symmetry
vocabulary.example: There is an asymmetry in the distribution of resources between the two departments.

vocabulary.definition: relating to or characterized by inertia; non-accelerating
vocabulary.example: An inertial reference frame is one in which a body remains at rest or moves with constant velocity unless acted upon by an external force.

vocabulary.definition: the process of becoming smaller or more compressed
vocabulary.example: According to special relativity, length contraction occurs when objects move at relativistic speeds.

vocabulary.definition: the speed of something in a given direction
vocabulary.example: The velocity of the spaceship increased as it approached the speed of light.

vocabulary.definition: a concept that combines the three dimensions of space and the one dimension of time into a single four-dimensional continuum
vocabulary.example: In the theory of general relativity, spacetime is curved by the presence of mass and energy.
